$comment: D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC-MONOMORPH-I32: runtime witness that the `<stdatomic.h>` OBJECT SURFACE works at widths other than `int`, across the legs, RUN on BOTH the baseline (debug) AND the `release` (shippedPipeline) arm. The `_Atomic` QUALIFIER was never truncated; it was the ACCESSOR surface that was monomorphized to i32, because a builtin config row carries ONE fixed signature text while C defines these as GENERIC functions (§7.17.1p6) — `atomic_store_explicit(&aLong, …)` was refused S_TypeMismatch while gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 both compiled and ran it. The fix DECLARES the shape (`genericPointee` in sources/c.lang.json): the row's signature is an exemplar and the real one is derived per call site from the argument's pointee. 52 distinct non-42 exits cover the qualifier at 64 bits, the shipped 64-bit object typedefs, the generic non-`_explicit` accessors incl. `atomic_init` (which is spelled as an assignment and therefore IS a seq_cst atomic store here — conforming under C23 §7.17.2.1, whose p3 makes concurrent access during initialization a data race, so the stronger form is unobservable; an earlier draft of this sentence claimed it was a PLAIN assignment and that was false), the RMW family above 32 bits, sub-word char/short/bool (the byte/half store_seqcst/load_acquire/store_release encoding slots, previously absent — `_Atomic char c; c = 1;` died at the ENCODER with A_NoMatchingEncodingVariant at width 8 — plus the integer PROMOTION the RMW ALU step takes because neither target declares a byte/half ALU form), an unsigned object, a data-model-dependent `_t` typedef, compare_exchange on a 64-bit object in BOTH outcomes, an atomic OBJECT POINTER (a type `_Generic` could never enumerate), and a ONE-BYTE compare-exchange flanked by NON-ZERO guard bytes. Those guards are load-bearing: a CAS that used the register-plumbing width instead of the memory-access one emitted `lock cmpxchg QWORD PTR` over a one-byte object and clobbered seven bytes of its neighbours — with zero neighbours the program still exits 42 and the miscompile is invisible. ★★ P64 ADDED THE SIGNED SUB-WORD ARMS AND THEY EXIST BECAUSE THE FIRST CUT OF THIS EXAMPLE MISSED A SILENT WRONG ANSWER: every sub-word CAS here used NON-NEGATIVE values, so a compare-exchange whose in-CAS compare ran at the CONTAINER width passed — while `_Atomic signed char` against `-1` under `--config=release` on arm64 returned `true` WITHOUT EXCHANGING, on a path that used to REFUSE loudly. A MATERIALIZED NEGATIVE constant is the whole witness. Also added: an ARRAY in the generic accessors' binding position (bare name and `arr + n`, both of which C 6.3.2.1p3 decays and both references run), and atomic POINTER arithmetic at TWO different element sizes — C §7.17.1p6 makes the operand `ptrdiff_t` and §7.17.7.5 makes the computation the `+` operator, so it is SCALED; gcc computes it unscaled and clang scaled, and the standard text settles it against gcc. EVERY value that can exceed 32 bits does: a value that fits would survive a silently-lost specialization unharmed and prove nothing. exit = 42.
